findings.issue: The table map contradicts A10, A12, A16 and A09, all edited on the same day, so a build that follows A04 breaks those nodes or two shapes co-exist. (a) A12 section 7 freezes `api_token.state` with the values pending_cosign, pending_owner_approval, active, held, revoked and expired. A04 has `status` with pending, active, suspended, revoked and expired, plus `pending_reason`, and says 'the names are A12's'. (b) A12 registers agent_counter, mandate_signing_key, agent_confirmation, agent_rate_bucket, agent_switch (all tiers, including platform) and agent_policy. A04 says three of these do not exist, makes agent_confirmation and mandate_usage core, and assigns agent_switch to A101. The registry then refuses A12's agent_confirmation, and A101 and A12 both register agent_switch. (c) A10 registers audit_anchor, audit_export and audit_partition itself, while A04 makes audit_anchor and audit_export core and adds audit_chain_head. A10 also still quotes A04's old column set (actor_label, object_type/object_id) and a global UNIQUE (prev_event_sha256). (d) A04 says vehicle-scoped ledger accounts carry the sponsor tenant 'as A16 states', but A16 says every ledger row is in the platform tenant, with sponsor_tenant_id as an attribute. (e) A09 lists 14 idempotency_key columns that A04 does not have, and has runtime service accounts use withPlatform rather than withSystem. A12's list of A04.1 columns (cosigner_*, row_version, hold_id, monthly caps, standing_consent_id, mandate_sha256, error_code, client_label) is absent too. So the pass criterion 'Fable's walk finds no missing column for A09, A10, A12 ... A16' fails on the first loop by construction.
findings.fix: Make one reconciliation pass that edits A04, A10, A12, A16 and A09 together. In A04 state each decision as final: api_token.status or state (pick one), with its exact enum values; which D04 tables are core and which are registered, and by which node; which audit tables A04 owns (anchor, export, chain head or partition); the ledger tenant model (A16's platform-tenant model, with sponsor_tenant_id and vehicle_id as attributes); A09's idempotency_key columns; A12's A04.1 columns folded into the core tables. Remove every opposite statement from the other specs. Add Data/schema-ownership.json (table, owner, shaping node, columns) generated from A04's map. Have the Fable walk compare every node spec against that file, so a contradiction fails the plan check and not the build.

findings.issue: The audit_event read policy can tip off an AML subject, and it gives investor-session writes no path. The class is 'class 1 plus a subject rule': an investor sees every event whose subject_investor_id is their own, and a sponsor sees every event in its tenant. There is no visibility or need-to-know column. So audit events about an AML alert, an AML case, an SMR decision or a freeze reason, written with the investor as subject, are readable by that investor and by the sponsor. That breaks N08 and the AML/CTF Act tipping-off rule, which class 7 protects for aml_case but not for the audit trail about it. A10 asks for exactly this (visibility subject_visible | staff | need_to_know | security, need_to_know_acl, subject_principal_id, vehicle_id), but A04 does not have it. Also, class 1 grants investor sessions 'nothing', and the subject rule is not stated to cover INSERT. So every audit write inside an investor or investor-agent transaction fails WITH CHECK, or the builder moves audit writes out of the business transaction.
findings.fix: Add visibility (an enum, NOT NULL), need_to_know_acl (a text[] required by CHECK when visibility = need_to_know), subject_principal_id and vehicle_id to audit_event. Write the audit_event policy as A10 item 7 describes: separate SELECT clauses per session kind, and a never-clause for need_to_know and security rows outside the ACL, the subject included. Give an explicit INSERT WITH CHECK (tenant, sandbox, actor_id or on_behalf_of_id = the session principal) that works for investor and agent sessions. Add RLS tests: investor X cannot see an aml_case-subject event about X; the sponsor cannot see it; support cannot see it; MLRO can.

findings.issue: A04 knows four principal types (HUMAN, PARTNER, AGNT, SVCA) and '52 roles', but A04 generates its enums from A03, its frozen dependency. A03 exports 51 roles and FIVE principal kinds, adding AGTU: 'a person's own agent acting through an API token (D04)', distinct from AGNT and 'never merged'. Every agent guard in A04 tests only 'AGNT': `CHECK (actor_type <> 'AGNT' OR on_behalf_of_id IS NOT NULL)`, the human-only trigger's `app.actor_type = 'AGNT'` clause, and agent_principal's 'own principal has type AGNT'. The generated enum will contain AGTU. So an AGTU audit event with no human behind it is accepted (the core D04 audit guarantee), and an AGTU agent_principal row is refused. Or the builder quietly relabels user agents as AGNT, which contradicts A03. A04's hard-coded counts (52 roles, 181 states) also differ from A03 (51 roles, plus AGT-U as a principal kind; 183 states once A03's extensions land), so any count assertion is wrong.
findings.fix: Define an agent-kind set generated from A03 ({AGNT, AGTU}) and use `actor_type NOT IN (agent kinds) OR on_behalf_of_id IS NOT NULL`, `app.actor_type IN (agent kinds)` and 'own principal kind in agent kinds' everywhere. Take the counts from A03's export instead of writing them into the spec. Add hidden and visible probes that repeat each AGNT probe with AGTU. Raise the AGNT/AGTU naming with A10, A11, A12 and A14 (none of them uses AGTU) in the reconciliation pass of finding 1.

findings.issue: The RLS classes use the same predicate for read and write ('Predicate (read and write)'). Under class 2, an investor session, or an investor's agent, can therefore INSERT or UPDATE its own register_entry, register_lot, holding, ledger_entry, distribution_line, tax_component, amma_statement, trade and allocation_line rows. Under class 3 it can write its own kyc_case, investor_classification, identity_claim, wallet_key, guardian and recovery_request rows. Under class 8 (owner = coalesce(on_behalf_of_id, principal_id)), an AGENT session can write its human's passkey, session, api_token and agent_mandate rows. Creating passkeys, creating or widening tokens, and changing guardians are D04 non-delegable acts, and the legal register and ledger must never be self-writable. The node says 'enforced by the schema, not by discipline', but only the app code stops these writes, and no test probes them.
findings.fix: Give each table a separate write class in RLS_CLASS: a read class and a write class. Write-protected tables (register_*, holding, ledger_*, distribution_*, tax_component, amma_statement, trade, allocation*, kyc_case, investor_classification, identity_claim, custody_*, approval_*) accept writes only from platform_access or named SVCA sessions. Add a trigger or WITH CHECK clause that refuses any write to passkey, session, api_token, agent_principal, agent_mandate, guardian, wallet_key, recovery_request and the withdrawal bank-account columns when app.actor_type is an agent kind. Add generated tests: an investor and an agent session cannot insert or update their own register, ledger, KYC or holding rows, and an agent session cannot insert a passkey, a token or a mandate.

findings.issue: The step-up assertion columns are only NOT NULL strings. created_with_assertion_id, approved_with_assertion_id, widened_with_assertion_id and agent_mandate.assertion_id reference nothing. A11 stores step-ups in a `fresh_assertion` row (principal, purpose, payload_sha256, consumed_at), but that table is not in A04's map, so no FK exists. Any non-null value satisfies 'a token with a null creation assertion is refused' and 'widening needs a new, different, non-null widened_with_assertion_id'. A fake or agent-supplied id passes both the build and Fable's oracle probes (i). So the database half of the non-delegable 'person present via passkey' rule can be satisfied with a fake.
findings.fix: Make `fresh_assertion` (and A11's nonce table) core tables shaped by A11, and insert-only apart from consumed_at, set once. Add FKs from every *_assertion_id column. Add a constraint trigger that requires: the assertion's principal equals owner_principal_id (or approved_by_principal_id for the approver); the principal kind is HUMAN or PARTNER; the purpose matches (token.create, token.widen, mandate.create); consumed_at is set in the same transaction; and one assertion is never reused for two rows. Add oracle and challenge probes that use a random id, another person's assertion, a reused assertion and a wrong-purpose assertion.

findings.issue: Maker-checker binding in the database stops at 'approval_id is non-null after state X' and 'custody_op.approval_id UNIQUE'. Nothing checks that the referenced approval_request is in the approved SM-00 state, that it is for this object and action, or that it is not reused. Two withdrawals (or two register instructions, allocations or halts) can cite one approval. A withdrawal in 'approved' can cite a rejected or expired approval, or one for another withdrawal. A custody_op can be inserted against an approval that is still pending, or whose payload hash differs from custody_op.calldata_sha256. A wrong build passes every listed CHECK and challenge (h), because they test only null and the duplicate custody op.
findings.fix: Add one constraint trigger for PRIVILEGED_TABLES and custody_op. It checks that the approval_request is in the SM-00 approved state (A03's name) at the moment the row enters its post-approval state, and that its object_ref equals the row, its action or policy code matches the table's entry in PRIVILEGED_TABLES, and its payload_sha256 equals custody_op.calldata_sha256 where it applies. Add a partial UNIQUE index on approval_id per privileged table, except where PRIVILEGED_TABLES declares a batch approval, such as distribution_run lines. Extend oracle item (h) with the probes: rejected approval, pending approval, another object's approval, one approval reused on two withdrawals, and a payload-hash mismatch.

findings.issue: Parts of the legal record and of the money book can still be changed in place. register_lot, which holds units and lock_in_until (the G08 lock-in), and register_instruction_line are ordinary mutable tables with updated_* and deleted_at. So a lot's units or lock-in date can be edited or soft-deleted with no history, which bypasses the bitemporal register that A18's invariant 'Σ register_lot.units = entry units' depends on. ledger_journal and ledger_snapshot are also mutable and soft-deletable. A16 says 'there is no update or delete path on journals or entries beyond reversed_by'. Other money rows (withdrawal, payment, distribution_line) carry deleted_at, and nothing says a soft delete is refused once they are post-approval.
findings.fix: Add register_lot (no allowed columns; a correction inserts lots under the successor entry), register_instruction_line and ledger_snapshot to INSERT_ONLY_TABLES. Add ledger_journal with only reversed_by, settable once. For money and legal tables that stay mutable, add a trigger refusing deleted_at once the row has left its draft state. Add these tables to the oracle's insert-only sweep (b) and to the 'Register history' challenge (an in-place update of lot units or lock_in_until).

findings.issue: Several triggers must read or write across RLS, but the spec gives them no privileged owner. FORCE RLS applies to realx_owner as well, and realx_definer (the only BYPASSRLS role) 'owns only the SECURITY DEFINER functions below', which are the five lookups. The cases: derive_tenant_from_vehicle must read vehicle rows that investor sessions cannot see (class 1 gives investors nothing). The ledger balance trigger must sum every entry of a journal, including class-1 rows with no investor that are invisible to an investor session. The AFTER INSERT trigger that maintains audit_chain_head writes a class-5 table from tenant and investor sessions. The human-only triggers read the maker's principal and approval_request. The register issue guard reads the allocation and the offering. audit_next_link is 'EXECUTE granted to realx_app only', so realx_worker jobs (recon, sweeps, the outbox relay) cannot write audit events. No search_path pinning is required for the SECURITY DEFINER functions, a known privilege-escalation path. The likely results are a build that fails, or a builder who weakens RLS to make the triggers work.
findings.fix: State that every guard, derive and chain trigger function is SECURITY DEFINER, owned by realx_definer, with `SET search_path = pg_catalog, public` (or the schema), and holds only the column-limited SELECT and UPDATE grants it needs, listed in a DEFINER_GRANTS constant that the tests read. Grant EXECUTE on audit_next_link to realx_worker too. Add a verify test that every SECURITY DEFINER function has a pinned search_path and is owned by realx_definer. Add RLS tests that run an order insert, a balanced journal and an audit write inside an investor session and an agent session.

findings.issue: The partner class cannot work as written. §4 says partners sign in at platform level (their app.tenant_id is the platform tenant), but class 4 requires `tenant_id = app.tenant_id AND vehicle_id = ANY(app.vehicle_scope)`, and vehicle rows carry the sponsor tenant id, so a partner sees nothing. A builder who instead sets app.tenant_id to the sponsor tenant confines a valuer, property manager or trustee-RE who serves two sponsors to one tenant per session. Class 1's 'for partner sessions, also class 4' can also be read as giving a partner every row of the tenant. The generated suite seeds only one partner, scoped to one vehicle of A, so neither defect is caught.
findings.fix: Define class 4 as `vehicle_id = ANY(app.vehicle_scope)` (the tenant integrity already comes from derive_tenant_from_vehicle), with vehicle_scope filled only by A98 from partner_engagement across tenants. State that class 1 gives partner sessions nothing beyond class 4. Seed a partner engaged by one vehicle of A and one vehicle of B, and assert that it sees exactly those two vehicles and nothing else in either tenant.

findings.issue: Two challenges have no matching build instruction, so the builder is not told to build what Fable will probe. First, 'A tenant_guardrail row with kyc_required = false' must be refused, but §3 defines no CHECK on tenant_guardrail. Second, 'two concurrent mandate_usage increments that both pass a cap' must fail, but A04 defines only UNIQUE (mandate_id, day) and leaves the cap comparison to A12's code, which does not exist at A04's gate.
findings.fix: Add to §3: `CHECK (kyc_required = true)` on tenant_guardrail, plus any other guardrail floors. Add a constraint trigger on mandate_usage that refuses cents_used > agent_mandate.daily_cap_cents and units_used > daily_units for the mandate version in force. Add a visible test for both, with a concurrent-increment test using two connections.
